title: Mitigating Privacy Risk via Forget Set-Free Unlearning
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Retaining data until unlearning finishes keeps users exposed to risk over time; deleting immediately on request removes the extra window of exposure.
layout: 2 stacked time-series panels, shared vertical event lines, left icons with risk surfaces
description: Two vertically stacked plots share a horizontal time axis t. Three vertical arrows run through both plots and mark events: user consents to add their data, user requests deletion, and unlearning completed. The top plot shows dataset risk R_D(t) as a wavy curve. The area under it is shaded blue-gray between consent and deletion, then red between deletion and unlearning completion. The bottom plot shows model risk R_M(t) as a wavy curve, with green shading from consent to unlearning completion. At left, each plot has a curved 3D mesh surface labeled 'Dataset Risk Vectors' or 'Model Risk Vectors'. A database cylinder icon sits on the top surface and a neural-network icon on the bottom one. Boxed labels point to the curves. The red region is the eye-catching element.
caption: Conventional unlearning algorithms admit a cumulative user risk totalling the sum of the \colorbox{f1brown-t}{green}, \colorbox{f1blue-t}{blue}, and \colorbox{f1red-t}{red} regions. By allowing user data to be deleted immediately once a request for deletion is made, Reload eliminates the user risk associated with the \colorbox{f1red-t}{red} region.
abstract: Training machine learning models requires the storage of large datasets, which often contain sensitive or private data. Storing data is associated with a number of potential risks which increase over time, such as database breaches and malicious adversaries. Machine unlearning is the study of methods to efficiently remove the influence of training data subsets from previously-trained models. Existing unlearning methods typically require direct access to the "forget set" -- the data to be forgotten-and organisations must retain this data for unlearning rather than deleting it immediately upon request, increasing risks associated with the forget set. We introduce partially-blind unlearning -- utilizing auxiliary information to unlearn without explicit access to the forget set. We also propose a practical framework Reload, a partially-blind method based on gradient optimization and structured weight sparsification to operationalize partially-blind unlearning. We show that Reload efficiently unlearns, approximating models retrained from scratch, and outperforms several forget set-dependent approaches. On language models, Reload unlearns entities using <0.025% of the retain set and <7% of model weights in <8 minutes on Llama2-7B. In the corrective case, Reload achieves unlearning even when only 10% of corrupted data is identified.
